images.caption:
Cows and Silage The pale fields in the distance have recently had a cut of silage taken off them but the bales of silage in the foreground are left over from last year. They have become rather mis-shapen with age and rank foliage has grown among them. There is an electric fence surrounding them so that the cows do not damage the thin polythene covering.
You can see the wind turbines on the skyline. The blades are not in full view because they are turned round to face the wind which is coming from the east.

images.filename: At the end of Llethri Road - geograph.org.uk - 945605.jpg
images.caption:
At the end of Llethri Road I always thought the farm here was very old but it doesn't appear on the 1940's old map. The farm known as Glyngwernan Uchaf is on the top of the hill and has panoramic views all around. 
In the trees at about (3 o'clock in the photo) is a disused quarry. It was a very scary place for children to play as it had a very eerie atmosphere and dangerous steep sides falling into deep black water below. We still played there - it had the best blackberry bushes for miles around!

images.filename: Behind bars - Swiss Valley School - geograph.org.uk - 945648.jpg
images.caption:
Behind bars - Swiss Valley School Built in 1970, replacing the old infant and junior schools in Felinfoel. It is in an amazing position with panoramic views sweeping east to west. The nearest building is an extension that did not exist when I was a pupil - we did have a portable cabin though, but it soon became evident that that wouldn't be sufficient for this popular, ever expanding school.
Mr Lewis was the headmaster, Mr Stan Phillips the deputy and some of the other lovely teachers when I was there were Miss Howells and Mr Morgan.

I would have liked to take more photos but in these times I decided it may not be wise to be seen taking photos of a school!

images.filename: Down Pennant hill, looking at Krupps Thyssen factory (once Fisher and Ludlow) - geograph.org.uk - 945547.jpg
images.caption: Down Pennant hill, looking at Krupps Thyssen factory (once Fisher and Ludlow) Situated on the eastern edge of Swiss Valley, this sprawling housing estate built in the 1960's and 1970's used to have a huge number of children playing in its roads. Now there are OAP's. Their families grown up and gone but most of the original occupants stayed. A good place to grow up.
